summary: Packed G32 integer CPU projections, a row-scaled FP8 host codec and the reference NVFP4 codec
implementation_scope: Grouped integer reference, native G32 signed 4/8-bit storage, scalar/optional AVX2 projections with optional dynamic int8 activations, plus a row-scaled FP8 host codec and oracle; NVFP4 codec (E2M1 codes, E4M3 block-16 scales, FP32 divisor, adjacent packing) with an FP64 Python oracle and a scalar C++ batched projection that decodes each block once per batch

agent_guidance.use_when: Use or adapt the grouped-integer codec, the row-scaled FP8 codec or the NVFP4 codec as the host reference of a format
agent_guidance.avoid_when: The artifact uses another block format or activation encoding; this is not a universal quantized tensor decoder
provides: Symmetric group quantization with represented FP32 scales
Signed byte/nibble packing, validation and dequantization
Host projection against finite unquantized activations and an optional backend hook
Validated borrowed G32 packed rows, native scalar/AVX2 projection and dynamically quantized int8 activation groups
Finite E4M3FN and BF16 word conversion, row-scale validation and independent host projection oracle
NVFP4 encode/decode with stated ties-to-even and saturation, adjacent packing and a batched scalar projection reference
engine_supplies: Actual artifact-format interpretation and any conversion
CPU feature dispatch and build flags for AVX2, other artifact codecs and device kernels for any of these formats; validated immutable payloads and numerical/quality criteria
Owned buffers, readiness and chosen numerical/quality criteria
preserve: Code packing, scale indexing and represented values agree
Group divisibility and exact packed extent
Arithmetic/rounding differences are explicit when porting or fusing
FP8 row scales are BF16 multipliers
NVFP4 packing layout and the divisor convention are explicit; no layout inference from sizes
adapt: Storage/arithmetic format as a separately declared codec
Activation quantization and accumulation with appropriate validation
The device kernel that runs a format, chosen through Kernels

code_files.purpose: Complete signed integer group codec with represented FP32 scales and host matrix-vector projection; other formats and optimized kernels are external
Native G32 packed row validation/encoding, row slices, scalar or AVX2 projection and optional int8 activation groups
Runnable portable W4/W8 and dynamic A8 projection with packed payload reporting
Portable BF16/E4M3FN codec, row conversion/validation and double projection oracle
NVFP4 codec and FP64 batched projection oracle
Header-only C++20 NVFP4 codec and scalar batched projection

requires.hardware: Python 3.11+ for the general integer reference; C++20 for native G32/FP8; optional CRIT_GROUPED_INT_AVX2 requires an AVX2 build and CPU
requires.model: Exact grouped-integer format or separately validated row-scaled E4M3FN/BF16 format; arbitrary artifact codecs need adaptation; NVFP4 with adjacent packing and a divisor global scale (convert other layouts explicitly)
requires.workload: Native G32 supports positive token batches, row-major tensors with width divisible by 32, FP32 or dynamic G32 int8 activations

contract.input: Finite rectangular weight rows and a finite activation vector; FP8 uses contiguous E4M3FN rows and represented BF16 row scales
contract.output: QuantizedRows codes/scales and projected row values; native FP8 returns double host oracle values
contract.ownership: Weight bytes and scales are immutable. An asynchronous backend must retain them and activations until its receipt settles.
contract.failure: Reject incomplete groups, invalid byte extents, nonfinite/unrepresentable scales and mismatched activation geometry. callers own payload validation, numerical overflow checks and physical settlement after partial failure.
contract.core_boundary: Keep quantization, encoding and arithmetic in consumer code; use core-owned workspace and backend services.

validation.host: Host fixtures and worked example cover signed/odd nibble packing, zero groups, scale representation and projection geometry; native tests cover every finite FP8 code, ties, zero/subnormal scales, odd extents and invalid words; native G32 fixture compares 108 scalar/SIMD projection profiles to independently reconstructed arithmetic, signed minimum codes, ties, invalid scales/extents and encoded-KV ownership; NVFP4 Python and native fixtures cover all E2M1 codes, every finite E4M3 code, ties, saturation, zero blocks, packing, error bounds and batched projection against FP64
validation.native: The native codec fixtures above run on the host; device kernels for these formats are chosen and measured by the engine
validation.performance: Kernel and model speed require matched consumer measurements; an AVX2 build alone establishes no speedup
